articles.title: Sunday Summary: Who’s Funding $1.3 Trillion in Data Center Spending?
articles.narrative: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the commercial real estate market, highlighting the explosive growth in data center investment, which has reached $1.3 trillion. It also notes a resurgence in the office sector, particularly in New York City, driven by AI firms, and continued strength in retail and multifamily markets across various regions. The piece draws on data from Atrium, Skanska, CBRE, Colliers, SitusAMC, Hoya Capital, and NAI Capital to support its observations on market trends and investment activity.
articles.market_intelligence: New York City has surpassed San Francisco as the largest tech labor market in North America, with 394,300 tech jobs compared to San Francisco's 375,730. Office investment conditions are improving, with the share of investors favoring office nearly tripling to 11 percent in Q2 2026 from 4 percent in Q2 2025. REIT earnings results were strong, with broad guidance raises and improving property-level fundamentals. Los Angeles real estate investment jumped 28 percent in July, primarily driven by housing.

articles.title: Inland completes equity raise for QOZ project in downtown St. Paul
articles.narrative: Inland Real Estate Investment Corporation has successfully completed an approximately $28 million equity raise for its Qualified Opportunity Fund, which holds an 89% ownership interest in a 16-story building at 386 Wabasha St. North in downtown St. Paul, MN. The property is undergoing an adaptive reuse conversion from an underutilized office building into a 178-unit multifamily residential community named "The Stella," which will also include street-level retail space. This project aligns with the evolving market dynamics and the increasing demand for urban living, contributing to the revitalization of downtown St. Paul.

data_points.address: 386 Wabasha St. North, St. Paul, MN
data_points.notable_features: Located in a Qualified Opportunity Zone, with direct access to the Saint Paul Pedestrian Skyway System and proximity to regional transportation, employment hubs, dining, entertainment, and cultural amenities.
data_points.project_notes: The project is an adaptive reuse of an office building into multifamily and retail, supported by historic tax credits and other financing structures. This is the sixth project completed in partnership between Inland and Kaeding, with four involving ground-up development or adaptive reuse.

articles.title: Davis acquires four-building outpatient medical portfolio in Minnesota
articles.narrative: Davis has acquired a four-building outpatient medical portfolio totaling 114,346 square feet from Lakeview Clinic for $31.3 million. The properties are located across Waconia, Norwood, Chaska, and Watertown, Minnesota. This sale-leaseback transaction allows Lakeview Clinic to monetize its real estate assets while continuing its clinical operations at all locations through extended leases. The deal highlights the importance of creative transaction structures and market expertise in the current challenging capital markets environment.

data_points.project_notes: Lakeview Clinic extended its leases at each property as part of the sale-leaseback transaction.

articles.title: Continuing to bet on the Minneapolis-area industrial market
articles.narrative: Oppidan Investment Company has broken ground on Rogers Gateway, a 117,000-square-foot speculative industrial project in Rogers, MN, with an estimated cost of $15 million. The development, scheduled for completion in November 2026, aims to provide flexible space for a variety of industrial users, including warehouse, distribution, manufacturing, showroom, and office components. The project's strategic location with direct visibility and access to Interstate 94 is a key selling point, capitalizing on the strong demand for new industrial construction in the growing northwest Twin Cities submarket.

data_points.notable_features: Direct visibility and access from Interstate 94, designed for flexible configurations to accommodate various tenant sizes and operational needs.
data_points.project_notes: Speculative development without a tenant in place.

articles.market_intelligence: The Minneapolis-area industrial market continues to show strong demand for new construction, particularly in well-located areas with strong highway access, visibility, and flexibility for various industrial users. The northwest Twin Cities is identified as one of the strongest submarkets for industrial leasing activity, driven by access to I-94, population growth, and connectivity to broader regional markets.

articles.title: Why Hines Is Restarting Its Development Engine
articles.narrative: Hines is strategically shifting its focus back to development, a move driven by the current slowdown in real estate investment volumes. The firm aims to capitalize on markets where scarcity of new product can command higher profits, indicating a proactive approach to market challenges by creating value through new construction rather than relying on existing asset transactions.
articles.market_intelligence: Real estate investment volumes are faltering, creating opportunities in scarcity-driven markets.
